newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM says ahead of 1996/97 output target.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM says ahead of 1996/97 output target.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM) said on Friday its production of copper and cobalt was ahead of target for the 1996/97 financial year.
ZCCM technical director John Patterson told Reuters production was slightly ahead of target in the first seven months of the financial year which began in April.
"We've been slightly ahead of the production target for both copper and cobalt," Patterson said in an interview.
Figures for the seven months are not yet available. The company produced some 164,000 tonnes of copper and about 2,450 tonnes of cobalt in the first six months of the financial year.
Patterson said the production target for the year was 335,000 tonnes of finished copper and 4,650 tonnes of cobalt.
He said working costs were also contained to within the budget.
ZCCM had been affected by the plunge in London Metal Exchange copper prices since June, Patterson said.
"We have of course as a company been somewhat hurt by the goings on at the London Metal Exchange in June with the Sumitomo affair and the consequent reduction of copper prices.
"That has made life difficult for us at the moment and we have to manage our expenditure commitments in line with the receipts that we are getting from this lower copper price," Patterson said.
He said cobalt production had become very important to ZCCM.
"Cobalt is a very important factor to us, it has seen a better price profile than copper and fortuanately we have been ahead of our production of finished cobalt.
"We will probably have the best cobalt year this year that we probably ever had," Patterson said.
The Zambian government has offered ZCCM for sale as part of its privatisation programme and 39 companies have pre-qualified to buy the mining and power assets of the company.
